topic: How do GEO vs LEO satellite orbits affect latency and coverage in hybrid networks for rural substation monitoring?
consensus_response: GEO offers fixed, high-capacity links with predictable connectivity but suffers from longer latency due to its altitude.  LEO satellites provide near real-time data transmission via lower latency but may experience varying signal strength depending on their orbital position. Hybrid networks leverage both GEO's stable coverage and LEO's low latency through redundant communication paths for optimal performance, balancing fixed and variable coverage needs. Dynamic routing protocols optimize network resilience by adjusting data packet routes based on real-time conditions.
reference_context: Satellite communications are key to smart grids, enabling reliable power monitoring and grid management.  GEO offers high capacity but long latency. LEO provides lower delay but higher costs for deployment. Hybrid networks integrate both for optimal performance in rural areas.
